subject: Demo follow-up: data sovereignty, prompt/output storage, and logging
messages:

Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>

Subject: Demo follow-up: data sovereignty, prompt/output storage, and logging

Hi Emily,

Thanks again for taking the demo earlier today. Quick recap and answers to the items you flagged so we have a single source of truth:

- What we demoed: hosted inference flow, optional Dedicated deployments, and the Redwood Console for per-route observability.
- High-level data model: inputs (prompts), generated outputs, and telemetry (latency, token counts). We treat each category differently for retention and access.

Immediate clarifications we discussed (short answers):
1) Do we persist raw prompts or outputs? By default, in our Hosted product prompts and outputs are not retained permanently. Non-PII telemetry is retained for 30 days for operational and quality purposes. Full-text prompts/outputs are only persisted if the customer enables data logging for debugging or explicitly opts in to analytics.
2) Can you choose residency? Yes — Hosted offers per-region tenancy (US/EU/APAC) and Dedicated/Private lets you control where data resides.
3) Audit and logs: Audit logs and request logs exist; access to identifiable request logs is restricted to a small set of authorized engineers and can be disabled/limited for customers that require it.

Next steps (proposal):
- I attached a short PII-handling matrix and a SOC2 extract for your security team to review.
- Can Procurement share the minimal DPA language they require? Legal can join a call.
- Proposed meeting: Wed 8/18 10:00am PT for procurement + security deep-dive.

I'll follow up with clarifying bullets in a second message to your specific retention and encryption questions.

Thanks,
Vivek Kulkarni
Head of Sales Engineering
Redwood Inference
(Attachment stubs: PII-handling-matrix.xlsx, Redwood_SOC2-extract.pdf)

Hi Vivek,

Thanks for the recap — helpful. A few specific questions from Security and Procurement so we can move this along: 

1) Do you store verbatim user prompts anywhere by default (searchable text store)?
2) Are generated outputs stored and indexed by default (for search/analytics)?
3) For hosted customers, what are the default retention windows for request logs vs telemetry vs full-text artifacts? We've seen 30/90/365 day asks and need your exact defaults.
4) If we opt out of hosted logging, do you still retain any model-level telemetry that could be linked to content?
5) Encryption: at-rest encryption and customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM) — do you support CMK for Dedicated/Private?
6) Residency: we need assurance records showing that logs and artifacts for US tenants remain in the US region.

Can you provide short, plain answers we can pass to Legal/Procurement as part of our vendor assessment? Also please attach any short evidence (SOC2 pages, DPA snippet).

Best,
Emily Carter
Senior Product Manager, NovaHealth

Hi Emily — great questions. Below are concise, actionable answers you can share with Procurement and Legal. If they want an annotated evidence pack we can provide that after a short call.

1) Raw prompts: Hosted default = we do not persist full-text prompts indefinitely. Operational debugging logs may contain prompts for up to 30 days by default. Customers may opt-in to longer-term logging for analytics or debugging; that is explicit and requires customer action. For Dedicated/Private, prompt storage is under customer control (you decide retention).

2) Generated outputs: Same model as prompts — not retained permanently in Hosted unless the customer enables result logging. We classify outputs as potential PII and treat them conservatively for retention/escape controls.

3) Retention windows (defaults, Hosted):
   - Operational telemetry (metrics, token counts, latencies): 30 days
   - Request logs (redacted by default): 30 days; full-text request logs are only kept when enabled for debugging and then retained per the enabled window (configurable).
   - Audit logs (account-level changes, admin actions): 365 days (configurable for enterprise customers).

4) Opt-out behavior: If you opt out of hosted request logging, we still retain non-identifying telemetry (metrics) needed for platform stability. Identifiable request logs are not retained if logging is disabled.

5) Encryption and keys:
   - In transit: TLS 1.2+ across all endpoints.
   - At rest: AES-256 encryption.
   - CMK support: Yes for Dedicated/Private deployments; hosted customers may use provider-managed keys or request CMK in select enterprise plans (we can scope during contracting).

6) Residency guarantees: For Hosted US tenancy, persisted artifacts and logs live in US data centers. For stronger guarantees (e.g., no logs leaving region under any circumstance), we recommend Dedicated or Private deployment where controls are customer-managed.

7) Access controls and support: Access to request logs that contain full-text is restricted to a named small group of engineers, and we provide audit entries for support access. Customers can require session recordings or support requests to be disabled.

Attachments: I re-attached the PII-handling matrix and a 1-page SOC2 extract. I've also dropped a short Drive link with an evidence pack we can expand on request: https://drive.google.com/open?id=1a2b3cPII-matrix

Suggested next steps:
- Procurement & Legal call (30–45m) to review DPA language and residency clauses — proposed Wed 8/18 10:00am PT.
- If Legal wants an evidence pack (SOC2 pages, encryption architecture diagram, sample audit log), we'll prepare and share within 48h.

If you want, Aditya (copied) can do a 20m technical deep-dive on encryption and the retention controls before the procurement call.

Best,
